newsitem.title: USA: Smallish U.S Nov trade gap seen boosting Q4 qrowth.
newsitem.headline: Smallish U.S Nov trade gap seen boosting Q4 qrowth.

text.p: Coming on the heels of a very respectable import-export performance in October, the narrow U.S. trade deficit in November will prompt upward revisions to U.S. growth forecasts, economists said.
On Friday the U.S. trade gap was reported up 4.9 percent to $8.4 billion in November from a revised $8.01 billion in October. Economists had expected a November gap of $9.8 billion.
"This will very likely boost fourth-quarter (gross domestic product) to 4.0 pct or even a little higher," said Richard Koss, international economist at MFR Inc.

Taken together, the 4.2 percent jump in October exports followed by the 0.3 percent export gain in November should result in upward revisions to GDP forecasts for the final three months of 1996, economists said.

"We managed to hold on to the gains we made in exports in October and that is impressive, given that the dollar is higher, as well as given the relatively slow growth path in most of our trading partners," Koss said.
Exports rose 0.3 percent to $71.97 billion in November, but imports increased 0.8 percent to $80.37 billion, leading to the slight deterioration in the overall trade deficit.
